```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Load the data
```{r}
kev<-
  read_csv(here::here("data/raw/kev/kev_2026-10-26.csv"))
```

## 1. Basic Checks
```{r}
glimpse(kev)
```

```{r}
colSums(is.na(kev))
```
No values are missing in the columns used below. Only `cwes` has gaps: 175 of 1756 entries (10%)

```{r}
summary(kev)
```

```{r}
kev |> count(knownRansomwareCampaignUse)
```
361 of 1,756 KEV entries (20.6%) are known to have been used in ransomware campaigns. The rest are marked "Unknown", which means no confirmed evidence, not that they were never used.

## 2. Entries added per year
```{r}
kev |> count(year = year(dateAdded))
```
KEV launched in November 2021 with 311 entries in its first two months, peaked at 555 in 2022, then settled near 190 a year in 2023-24. Additions are rising again: 2026 already has 272 by 23 October, more than all of 2025 (245).

```{r}
kev |>
  count(year = year(dateAdded)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2021:2026) +
  labs(title = "KEV additions peaked in 2022, dipped and are rising again",
       subtitle = "2026 is up to 23 October",
       x = NULL, y = "CVEs added to KEV")
```

## 3. Top 15 vendors
```{r}
top15<- kev |> count(vendorProject, sort = TRUE) |> head(15)
top15
```
Microsoft products account for the most KEV entries: 390 out of 1756 (22%), more than Cisco, Apple and Adobe combined (278)

```{r}
sum(top15$n)
round(100 * sum(top15$n) / nrow(kev), 1)
```
Top 15 vendors make up 1046 out of 1756 entries (59.6%)

```{r}
top15 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = fct_reorder(vendorProject, n))) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "15 out of 291 vendors make up over half of the total entries (59.6%)",
       x = "CVEs in KEV", y = NULL)
```
